protocol.Account: Account is one provider account this User holds. Adding a provider adds a vocabulary rather than a field (ADR-030).
protocol.Account.binding: What proves this account belongs to a key this User holds. Without it the list above is an assertion, and the proof lives only in a browser.
protocol.Account.canonical_id: What that provider calls the account — Mastodon a profile URL, atproto a DID. It comes from the provider, or the binding was not signed.
protocol.Account.handle: What the account calls itself. Display only.
protocol.Arrival: What a stand records when somebody arrives (ADR-035). The shape is the industry's: Plausible's `events_v2` and Umami's `website_event` agree on nearly all of it, and site analytics is finished work.
protocol.Arrival.at: When the stand fired. The only field the node authors, because it is the only one the visitor cannot claim.
protocol.Arrival.bot: What the node decided rather than read. A hit from a bot still happened; only the judgement is ours.
protocol.Arrival.browser: Derived at ingest from a user agent the node then drops. Nobody stores the raw string: it identifies, it is unbounded, and this is what gets queried.
protocol.Arrival.country: Derived at ingest from an address the node then drops. The answer is what gets asked for; the source of it is what identifies a person.
protocol.Arrival.event: The event the pixel side named. Naming none is a page view, and page_view is Google's word for it — borrowed, so a site firing gtag needs no translation, rather than a word the node invented.
protocol.Arrival.language: The language the browser asked in.
protocol.Arrival.market: The stand. Every other tool calls this site_id.
protocol.Arrival.params: What the site attached, verbatim. The node never learns what a key means — the line between analytics for anyone and analytics for one customer.
protocol.Arrival.path: The page. Path is what gets grouped, query is read once.
protocol.Arrival.referrer_domain: Split on arrival. Grouping by domain is the question people ask, and a whole URL answers it only after being taken apart again every time.
protocol.Arrival.screen: Sent by the snippet, because a server cannot see it. A bucket rather than a pixel count, by convention.
protocol.Arrival.utm_source: The campaign five. Fields rather than params because every tool and every ad platform already agrees on these names.
protocol.Arrival.visit: One sitting, ending when the tab does. Umami carries both ids; without this one a person is a single visit forever.
protocol.AsyncJob:
AsyncJob is one job as the browser receives it, mirroring async.Job.

Distinct from queue.proto's Job, which is the same concept over gRPC. They are two encodings and not one: gRPC carries timestamps as int64 and the payload as bytes, and the JSON a browser reads carries RFC3339 strings and the payload as an object. ADR-006 names this — proto's type model does not match the JSON API on timestamps — and a message that claimed both would be wrong about one of them.
protocol.AsyncJobProgress: AsyncJobProgress is how far along one job is.
protocol.AsyncJobPulseState: AsyncJobPulseState is the rate limit and budget state carried with a job.
protocol.AttestationCommand: AttestationCommand is used for creating attestations
protocol.Binding: Binding is the node's signature over "this key holds this account", the halves not already on the Account it proves (`laye-binding/v1`, ADR-030).
protocol.Binding.issued_at: When it was signed. Part of the canonical bytes, so it is not decoration.
protocol.Binding.peer_pubkey_hex: Which of the User's keys the claim is about.
protocol.Binding.signature_hex: The signature over provider, canonical_id, handle, peer_pubkey and issued_at, in that order.
protocol.Binding.signer_pubkey_hex: Who signed. Storing this is not storing a verdict: a binding is worth whatever `auth.binding_signers` says at the moment it is used, and this is the field that question is asked about.

protocol.Staand:
Staand is one stand as the stands element sees it. Beyond what it is (slug, namespace, URL) it carries its defining system attestation — the ASID, when it was created, and the DID that created it — the door it inherits from its namespace, the sites reporting back, and its activity: arrivals recorded against arrivals the rate limit refused, and when the last landed.

defId and lastSeen are named as the view has always read them.

protocol.StaandMetrics.market: The market that was asked about.
protocol.StaandMetrics.slug: The stand that was asked about.
protocol.StaandMetrics.type: What the arrivals were grouped by.
protocol.StaandSeen: StaandSeen is an event or a page and every moment it was attested, in unix milliseconds. "The axis of time is more useful than a tally": the view draws these as a line over time, and a count is not sent.
protocol.StaandSeen.seen: A JSON number, as the view reads it: protojson writes a 64-bit integer as text, and a millisecond is exact in a double.
protocol.StaandStep: StaandStep is one arrival read as a step rather than as a number: when it landed, the page it was about, and the event the pixel named.
protocol.StaandTakenDown: StaandTakenDown is what staands take-down answers.
protocol.StaandTakenDown.slug: The stand that was taken down.
protocol.StaandVisits: StaandVisits is what staands visits answers.
protocol.StaandVisits.market: The market that was asked about.
protocol.StaandVisits.slug: The stand that was asked about.
protocol.StaandVisits.visits: One row per sitting: who, when it started and ended, how long, the first and last page, how many views and events, and whether it was a bounce.
protocol.StaandWalk: StaandWalk is one person's steps past the stand, in the order they took them. The visitor id is theirs and persists (the snippet keeps it in localStorage), so this is a person's whole path across every visit, not one sitting.
protocol.Staands: Staands is what staands list answers.
protocol.Staands.staands: One row per stand that has not been taken down.
protocol.Standing: Standing is what i standing and i step answer.
protocol.Standing.namespace: Where the person now stands. Never empty.
protocol.SystemCapabilitiesMessage: SystemCapabilitiesMessage is what the node tells a fresh connection about itself: which store it keeps and which implementations are behind it. Mirrors syscap.Message.
protocol.SystemCapabilitiesMessage.parse: wasm or go: which parser implementation is active.
Whether it is ats through WASM.
protocol.SystemCapabilitiesMessage.stora: rust or go: which storage implementation is active.
Whether it is the Rust SQLite one.
protocol.SystemCapabilitiesMessage.store: store is which store the node keeps (ADR-023) — sqlite or parquet. Distinct from storage_backend, which is the implementation behind it. Namespaces exist only under parquet, and sigma only under sqlite.
protocol.TaskInfo: A task within a stage, with its log count.
protocol.Transcript: Transcript is one agent session Ground recorded, derived from its hook events: transcripts read answers these.
protocol.Transcript.effort: The effort its last Stop ran at, as that Stop's effort.level says.
protocol.Transcript.folded: Events the store folded into sigmas (ADR-020), counted and not read.
protocol.Transcript.model: The model the session started on, as its SessionStart says.
protocol.Transcript.turns: Its turns, each naming the attestation it was read from.
protocol.Transcripts: Transcripts is what transcripts read answers.
protocol.Transcripts.transcripts: Each session: its id, the subjects it was about, when it started and ended, and its turns, each naming the attestation it was read from.
protocol.Turn: Turn is one thing said or done in a session, naming the attestation it was read from.
protocol.Turn.at: When it was said or done.
protocol.Turn.of: The attestation it was read from.
protocol.Turn.speaker: Who said or did it.
protocol.User: A User is a human being (ADR-031). Nothing recorded one before this file: every place the system meant a User it stored a way to reach one, so the same User reached by two routes was two strings with nothing joining them.
protocol.User.accounts: One per provider that named one. A provider names an account its own way.
protocol.User.created_by: The ROOT User is to name the node that signed its first admission, which is bootstrap work; until then it is empty, and that is how ROOT is told apart.
protocol.User.disabled_at: Disabled and deleted are different: the record stays, and enabling it again is the same switch turned back. A disabled User cannot log in, and what they minted is disabled with them.
protocol.User.disabled_by: Which User turned the switch. A person is not disabled by nobody.
protocol.User.display_name: What this person calls themselves, set when they first arrive and never blank. It is the name segment of the id above, and the only handle a User has that no provider issued.
protocol.User.email_addresses: Any number of each (ADR-031). Repeated is the statement: neither one tells one User from another.
protocol.User.first_name: A User has a first name and a last name (ADR-031). Two fields because the ADR names two things.
protocol.User.id: An ASUID under `US` (ADR-010): `US-TIM-7K4M3B9X`. The name segment is what was known at minting, for reading in a log; uniqueness is the suffix, so a person renaming themselves does not restate who they are.
protocol.User.keys: laye mints one per browser and an authenticator derives one per device, so a User holds several and none of them is the User (ADR-030).
protocol.User.level: What this User may do (ADR-027). Says how much, never where.
protocol.VaultDirs: VaultDirs is what vault dirs answers.
protocol.VaultDirs.dirs: Each folder's place in the vault, folders apart by /.
protocol.VaultRepos: VaultRepos is what vault repos answers.
protocol.VaultSubdirs: VaultSubdirs is what vault subdirs answers.
protocol.VaultSubdirs.branch: The repository's default branch, which the folders are read on and a folder is bound to.
protocol.VaultSubdirs.dirs: Each folder's path from the repository's top.
protocol.VersionInfo: VersionInfo is which build is running, as am version answers it. Mirrors version.Info.
protocol.VersionInfo.go_version: The Go it was built with.
protocol.Visit: One sitting, derived from the arrivals carrying its visit id. Nothing writes a Visit — it is a projection and the arrivals stay the record, the same way Plausible maintains sessions as a view over its event table.
protocol.Visit.bounce: One arrival and gone. A convention, not a measurement: defining it differently makes the number incomparable to everyone else's.
protocol.Visit.entry_path: The two pages worth naming out of however many they saw.
protocol.Visit.started: Duration is the difference, carried because it is asked for constantly and derived identically by everyone.
protocol.WatcherBroadcastStats: WatcherBroadcastStats is what one watcher has done, carried in queue status.
protocol.WatcherFire: WatcherFire is one thing that happened to a watcher: when, and what caused it. An id alone cannot be drawn as a result row, so the attestation rides along when the store still holds it. omitempty in Go is absence on the wire, so a field the API may leave out is declared optional here. A browser told a field is always there reads undefined off an object that never carried it.
protocol.WatcherQueueStatusMessage:
WatcherQueueStatusMessage is the execution queue as the browser sees it.

A map field cannot be marked optional in proto3; target_elements and watcher_stats are omitempty in Go, so the wire carries no key when empty.
protocol.WatcherRegistration: WatcherRegistration declares a watcher a plugin wants core to manage. Core creates/updates the watcher on Initialize and routes matches to the plugin via ExecuteJob.
protocol.WatcherResponse:
WatcherResponse is a watcher as /api/watchers answers for it.

Mirrors server.WatcherResponse: Go keeps its own struct for the json tags (ADR-006), and the browser's shape is declared here.
protocol.WatcherResponse.action_type: What it does when something matches.
protocol.WatcherResponse.standing: standing marks a watcher the node is born with rather than one somebody made: held in no store, so it cannot be edited or deleted, and a reader looking at the list has to be able to tell which is which.
protocol.WatcherResponse.subjects: What it watches. A repeated field cannot be marked optional in proto3; these are omitempty in Go, so the wire carries no key at all when a watcher names no dimension. Read them as possibly absent.
protocol.WatcherResponse.warning: Set when a write succeeded but the engine did not take it, so a 200 cannot be read as "this watcher is now doing what you asked".
